meta.title: ThoxOS Ginux Edition 0.1.0
meta.subtitle: Ginux review, ThoxOS on an independent Rust kernel, Docker demo and KnightHub SSD image
meta.owner: Odette Lark, memory-sync node and fleet librarian
meta.closing: Research preview. Not for production use.

lede: ThoxOS now boots on Ginux, Gregory Kurtzer's Rust kernel that runs Linux programs with no Linux kernel underneath. In the Docker demo a ThoxOS userspace pulled from a private local registry reached systemd multi-user and the login prompt, and the ThoxOS shell ran typed commands on the Ginux kernel. An 8 GiB external-SSD image boots a Debian host that runs Ginux on tty1. Real hardware and KVM are the next gate.

blocks.text: Branch ginux-edition-0.1.0 of ttracx/thoxos-ginux, directory ginux-edition/. It sits beside, not over, the record a ChatGPT/Codex session pushed the same evening.

rows: thox ask sends prompts to any OpenAI-compatible server on the host through 10.0.2.2; thox status reports identity, kernel and endpoint. No model ships in the image.
Upstream Ginux at 36503bd with three patches: 48-bit IOMMU and firmware discovery, ThoxOS banner, and one per-build registry root accepted only for registry.thoxos.internal.
Rocky Linux 10 UBI init (the digest upstream validated) with a ThoxOS identity overlay: os-release, issue, motd, thox, thox-shell.
Read-only TLS registry and DNS forwarder on host loopback; thoxos-g owns the QEMU profile and drives the Ginux controller.
Serial console, browser console (ttyd, one client, generated credential), and tty1 on KnightHub.
8 GiB GPT image (systemd-boot, Debian 13 host, KVM launcher, first-boot growth), Linux writer with guards, Windows writer.

blocks.text: Ginux is real and runs Linux userspace. It is also a research prototype: virtio-only devices, one CPU, a 4 GiB identity map, a public development signing key and no security audit.

rows: QEMU before 9.1 uses a 39-bit IOMMU; Ginux panics
QEMU 10.0.13 panics in virtio-net init; 10.2 and 11.1 pass
Embedded minimal-system domain panics (stale auxv fixture check)
Guest RAM above 2.75 GiB panics (identity map)
Controller seal uses a public test key; no audit
Research-preview label; no guest ports exposed
Console has no line discipline: login and an interactive bash end at the first read
OCI cache answers by tag: a kept volume boots the previous build's userspace
Volume stamped with the manifest digest; replaced on change

blocks.title: Fit
blocks.text: High demo value, low product value today. THOX device kernels stay Linux; Ginux shows what one expert plus an agent can build.

items: Build: make ssd-image (or use the image from this delivery's build host).
Write to a spare USB SSD: installer/install-to-ssd.sh on Linux, or Install-ThoxOSGinux.ps1 or Rufus DD mode on Windows.
Disable Secure Boot, open the boot menu, choose the SSD.
tty1 shows ThoxOS; Ctrl-Alt-F2 is the host admin login (user thox, new password at first login).

blocks.title: Disk rule
blocks.text: The writer refuses the THOXOS-labeled 500 GB SSD that carries ThoxOS Vibe unless told to erase it. Use a spare SSD.

A ChatGPT/Codex session pushed a controller-only research record to main the same evening. It confirms the IOMMU width, the identity-map limit and the embedded-domain panic. This record adds the OCI userspace boot, the Docker run and the SSD image. One summary field there reads Linux domain execution failed; here the OCI domain passes and only the embedded path fails. docs/RECONCILIATION_2026-10-28.md lists every agreement and disagreement for a ruling.

nextSteps: Write the SSD image to a spare USB SSD and boot KnightHub; capture tty1 and thoxos-g doctor.
Rule on the two records and the SSD target (spare disk or ThoxOS Vibe host).
Open the upstream pull request for patch 0001 and issues for the QEMU 10.0, auxv and OCI cache findings.
